rows.why: S1 combines several questions: the BOM (item 9), the header (item 8), the row order (item 1) and CRLF on every line (item 10). Item 1 is the closest match because it asks the one question that is specific to S1's rows: their order. Its output sorts by creation time and then by id, which is what S1 expects. Items 8, 9 and 10 also agree: the output starts with U+FEFF, the header text is exact, and every line, the last included, ends in CRLF.

Item 7 asks how the Created column is formatted. S2 expects the UTC date as YYYY-MM-DD, but the call returned the full ISO timestamp, '2024-03-05T06:07:08.009Z'. No item asks how status is displayed, and the output also shows lowercase 'open' rather than 'Open'.
Item 11 asks how an empty list is exported. The call returned the BOM and header row alone, which is what S3 expects.

Item 12 asks how fields with separators are quoted. Its pick quotes only fields containing a comma, quote, CR or LF, with doubled quotes. S4 also requires quoting a title that starts or ends with a space, and the pick leaves those out.
Item 12 covers formula injection, and its pick says there is no guard. The call wrote '=SUM(A1)' unchanged, but S5 expects a leading single quote.

Item 6 asks whether a bad requisition fails the whole export, which is what S6 settles across all of its conditions. Items 2–5 each cover only one condition. The call threw an error naming 'bad' and returned no CSV, as S6 expects. Items 2–5 each also throw with the requisition id.
